Where Marketing & reviews goes wrong for Landscapers

Before-and-after photos are the most effective marketing a landscaping business has. Reviews that include them consistently outperform paid ads in local search.

What Landscapers jobs really involve

Landscaping runs on repeat visits and route density — the same properties, week after week. Scheduling and routing matter more than almost anything else, and most customers are happy to pay by card on the day.

Frequently asked questions

Which marketing & reviews tools work best for landscapers?

The three that fit best here are Canva Magic Studio (Trades producing their own flyers, social posts and quotes without a designer), Semrush (Businesses serious about ranking for local searches), ChatGPT (Everyone — it is the most flexible tool on this list). Start with the one whose description matches your crew size, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does marketing & reviews software cost for landscapers?

Across the 4 tools on this page, 4 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices change often, so treat the figures here as indicative and confirm on the vendor site.

Why does marketing & reviews cause problems for landscapers specifically?

Before-and-after photos are the most effective marketing a landscaping business has. Reviews that include them consistently outperform paid ads in local search.

Is per-visit or monthly billing better for landscaping?

Monthly billing suits recurring maintenance because it matches how customers budget. Per-visit works better for one-off cleanups and seasonal work where the scope changes each time.
